work: Subjects For Questioning About The Mourning Dress
heading: Liji 33 · Fu Wen 服問 · Subjects For Questioning About The Mourning Dress · Fu Wen 1 … Fu Wen 19

items.text: Wear deep mourning for your husband's mother, even if your husband wears only light.
items.quote: Such is the mourning for her husband's mother by the wife of the son of a ruler (by a concubine).

items.text: Wear only light mourning for your own mother if she was a concubine, while your wife wears deep.
items.quote: There are cases in which parties wear deep mourning, while those, in consequence of their connexion with whom they assume it, wear only light.

items.text: Wear light mourning for your wife's parents, while she wears deep.
items.quote: Such is the mourning of a husband for the father or mother of his wife.

items.text: Wear deep mourning for your own parents, even though your spouse wears light.
items.quote: There are cases in which parties wear light mourning, while those, in consequence of their connexion with whom they assume it, wear deep mourning.

items.text: Wear mourning for your husband's female cousins even though he wears none.
items.quote: Such is the case of the wife of a ruler's son with the cousins of her husband on the female side.

items.text: Do not wear mourning for your female cousins, though your wife does.
items.quote: There are cases in which parties wear mourning, while those, in consequence of their connexion with whom they have a relation with the deceased, wear none.

items.text: If you are a ruler's son, do not wear mourning for your wife's parents.
items.quote: Such is the case of a ruler's son with regard to the father and mother of his wife.

items.text: If your mother was divorced, wear mourning for the relatives of your father's second wife; if she died, mourn your own mother's relatives but not your stepmother's.
items.quote: When his mother has been divorced, the son wears mourning for the relatives of the wife whom his father has taken in his mother's place.

items.text: Preside at the mourning rites for your wife, eldest son, and daughter-in-law.
items.quote: A ruler acted as presiding mourner at the mourning rites for his wife, his eldest son, and that son's wife.

items.text: If your mother was a concubine, wear mourning for her; your ministers need not, but your personal attendants may follow you.
items.quote: When the mother of a ruler had not been the wife, the ministers did not wear mourning; only the officers of the harem and charioteer followed the ruler's example.

items.text: Do not put off your mourning headband when visiting others or at court; only at the ruler's gate may you put off sackcloth.
items.quote: In all cases of going to see others, the visitor (being in mourning for his parents) did not put off his headband.

items.text: Do not take away from others their mourning rites.
items.quote: A superior man will not take away from others their mourning rites.
